conclusion: The entropy/signature lane is closed by proof, not by difficulty: for every prime bound P, arbitrarily large sets satisfy every constraint S-summability imposes at primes below P (Theorem B), so no entropy, VC, container, DRC or forbidden-pattern argument over prime-valuation signatures can bound |A| at all, let alone beat 2^k. The salvage is Lemma A (for p not in S, A meets at most (p+1)/2 residue classes mod p, and |A| <= 2 when p = 2), which refutes the parent's loose thread '|A| <= p-1' and which, pushed to CRT injectivity, saves exactly one bit per absent prime and so lands quantitatively far short of Erdos-Turan.
confidence: Lean on Theorem B, Lemma A and the refutation as fully as on any two-line proof: they are short, self-contained, and each is checked computationally in probe.py (P=60 with |A|=200 and zero violations; the counterexample A={1,3,7,13}, S={2,5,7} re-verified by trial division). The scope claim around Theorem B is a judgment call and should be read as stated: it kills arguments whose input is p-adic data at a FIXED finite prime set, which is what the brief's tool list consumes; it does not kill an argument that uses the archimedean ordering or the cofinite condition. The numbers quoted for the ESS unit-equation route are recalled from the literature and were not re-derived here.
